title: Keyboard Hand Position
facts: The illustration contrasts correct and incorrect hand positions at a keyboard.
The correct examples show straighter wrists, while the wrong examples show wrists bent upward or sideways.

title: Average Rainfall
facts: The chart compares average rainfall in inches in four cities.
New York has the highest rainfall at 47.25 inches, followed by Dallas at 33.70.
Honolulu records 22.02 inches, while Phoenix has the lowest at 7.66.

title: India Land Use
facts: The map shows different types of land use across India.
The legend identifies arable land, forests, plantations, non-agricultural land, scrub and grass, and unproductive land.
The land-use patterns vary across the country.

title: Earth’s Structure
facts: The diagram illustrates the internal structure of Earth.
The labelled layers include the crust, mantle, outer core and inner core.
An inset distinguishes oceanic and continental crust and identifies the upper and lower mantle.

title: Bird Feeder
facts: The photographs show two bird feeders made from plastic bottles.
The bottles contain seeds and have perches inserted through their sides.
One feeder is shown with a bird using its perch.

title: Athletics Participation Survey
facts: The line graph compares boys and girls participating in high school athletics from 1971 to 2010.
Boys remain above girls throughout the period.
Girls participation rises strongly, while boys participation falls after an early peak and then increases again.
By the end, both groups are at their highest or near-highest levels.

title: Population Density
facts: The world map shows geographical differences in population density.
Dense concentrations appear in parts of Asia and Europe.
Large areas of northern regions, deserts and central Australia are less densely populated.

title: Trading Goods
facts: The diagram shows imports and exports associated with ancient Egypt.
Imports include timber, metals, ivory and animals from several regions.
Exports listed include linen, tools, beads, beer, weapons and oil.

title: Earth’s Climate Zones
facts: The map divides the world into polar, temperate and tropical climate zones.
The tropical zone lies around the equator between approximately 30 degrees north and south.
Temperate zones lie farther from the equator, while polar zones are near the poles.

title: International Student Funding
facts: The table compares primary funding sources for international students in the United States in 2003/04 and 2013/14.
Personal and family funding remains the largest source, with its share decreasing from 67 to 65 percent.
The total number of students rises from 572509 to 886052.
Funding from current employers and foreign governments or universities shows particularly large percentage increases.

title: Rainfall vs Temperature
facts: The combined chart shows monthly rainfall as bars and temperature as a line.
Temperature rises to a midyear peak and then declines.
Rainfall generally increases towards an autumn peak before falling again.

title: Australian Population Density
facts: The map shows the distribution of population across Australia.
Population is concentrated near the coast, especially in the east and southeast.
The interior has relatively few population dots, and major cities are labelled.

title: Australian Population
facts: The horizontal bar chart compares populations of Australian states and territories in 2006.
New South Wales has the largest population, followed by Victoria and Queensland.
The Northern Territory has the smallest population, followed by the Australian Capital Territory and Tasmania.

title: Population Doubling Time
facts: The graph plots the years required for world population to double against the ending year.
The early doubling period takes 544 years, whereas later intervals become much shorter.
The overall trend is a sharp decline in doubling time.

title: Quiz Process Flow
facts: The flowchart begins with clicking to start a quiz and then opening Question 1.
Clicking false leads to a correct-answer slide, while clicking true leads to a wrong-answer slide.
Both routes proceed to Question 2.

title: Pupil–Teacher Ratio
facts: The chart shows the distribution of pupil-to-teacher ratios in primary schools in January 1997.
The highest percentage occurs at a ratio of 24 pupils per teacher.
The smallest and largest ratio categories have lower percentages than the middle categories.

title: Sitting Posture
facts: The illustration compares correct and incorrect sitting posture at a desk.
The correct example shows a more upright position and supported feet.
The incorrect example shows the person leaning forward towards the screen.

title: Drinking Habits
facts: The stacked bar chart compares drinking habits across age groups in the United States.
The categories are heavy, light, former and never drinkers.
Former drinkers form a larger share in older groups, while light drinkers generally form a smaller share.

title: Closed-Loop Recycling
facts: The diagram presents a closed-loop plastics supply chain.
The stages are collecting and recycling, sorting and shredding, moulding and manufacturing, assembling and shipping, and purchasing and using.
The circular arrows show that used products return to the recycling process.

title: Homologies
facts: The diagram compares homologous structures in a human arm, seal forelimb, bird wing and bat wing.
The human example labels the hand, wrist, fingers, radius, ulna and humerus.
The limbs have different shapes and functions but share a related structural arrangement.

title: Laboratory
facts: The photograph shows two people working in a laboratory.
They wear laboratory coats and protective glasses.
They are handling glass containers containing liquid.

title: Climate Zones
facts: The map shows climate zones across Australia based on temperature and humidity.
The north includes hot and humid areas, while the south includes temperate areas.
Cool temperate conditions are shown in the far southeast and Tasmania.

title: US States
facts: The graphic compares five labelled places using horizontal pencil-shaped bars.
New Jersey has the largest displayed value at 50.680, followed by Chicago at 46.750.
Virginia has the smallest displayed value at 18.950.
The title says US States, although Chicago is included among the labels.

title: Average Rainfall
facts: The grouped bars compare rainfall in the United Kingdom, Japan and Australia across four seasons.
The United Kingdom is highest and Australia lowest in each season.
Rainfall is generally lower in winter than in spring or summer.

title: Population Density
facts: The map shows Australian population density in June 2010.
Density is highest in several coastal regions, particularly in the east and southeast.
Most of the interior has a low population density.

title: Tree Structure
facts: The diagram identifies the main parts of a tree.
Leaves, twigs and branches form the crown above the trunk.
Roots extend beneath the ground.

title: Number of Bonds
facts: The pie chart shows the number of bonds listed at the end of 2012.
Corporate bonds dominate with 740, followed by government bonds with 147.
Local government bonds and SME private debts each have 44, while the remaining categories are much smaller.

title: World Water Distribution
facts: The upper pie chart divides world water into 98 percent salt water and 2 percent fresh water.
The freshwater breakdown shows 87 percent ice, 12 percent groundwater and 1 percent rivers and lakes.
Most world water is saline, and most freshwater is stored as ice.

title: World Water Distribution
facts: The graphic divides global water into 97.5 percent salt water and 2.5 percent freshwater.
Most freshwater is in glaciers and permanent snow, followed by groundwater.
Only a small part is in other stores such as lakes, soil, rivers and living things.

title: Lecture Hall
facts: The illustration shows a lecture hall with rows of seats facing the front.
A central aisle leads towards a stage and a large presentation screen.
Windows and ceiling lights surround the room.

title: Adults vs Teens
facts: The grouped bars compare adults and teenagers by the number of texts sent on a typical day.
Adults most commonly send 1 to 10 texts, at 51 percent.
Teenagers are more strongly represented in the 101-plus category, at 29 percent compared with 8 percent for adults.
Adults have a larger share in the no-text category.

title: Garden Instructions
facts: The photograph shows a sign asking visitors to respect and enjoy historic gardens.
The symbols prohibit cycling, alcohol and a ball activity.
A person walking a dog is shown as permitted.

title: Ice Thickness
facts: The illustration presents minimum ice-thickness guidelines for new clear ice.
The labelled thicknesses increase from 4 inches for a person to 5–7 for a snowmobile, 8–12 for a car and 12–15 for a truck.
The heading states that ice is never 100 percent safe.

title: Iron Age Hut
facts: The cross-section shows an Iron Age hut.
The roof is labelled with rafters and reed thatch.
The interior includes a seat and ashes, while the sides include a turf wall and ground level.

title: Protective Equipment
facts: The illustration shows a worker surrounded by personal protective equipment symbols.
These include a helmet, hearing protection, protective glasses, a mask, gloves and boots.
The image emphasises several forms of workplace protection.

title: Weekly Household Spending
facts: The infographic compares average weekly household expenditure in 2015–2016.
Housing is the largest displayed category at 164 euros, followed by transport at 124 and food at 123.
Education and training is one of the smallest categories at 18 euros.

title: American Fast Food
facts: The grouped bar chart compares American fast-food dining frequency in July 2003, December 2006 and July 2013.
About once a week and once or twice a month are the largest frequency groups.
Every day and never are the smallest groups.
The once-or-twice-a-month category is highest in 2013.

title: Plastic Bottle Recycling
facts: The diagram shows a cycle for recycling old plastic bottles.
Used bottles are collected and processed through a recycling facility.
New bottles are produced and can return to the cycle after use.

title: Taxation by Countries
facts: The horizontal bar chart compares payroll and superannuation taxation by country.
Australia and Austria both show 16.6 percent at the top.
Denmark appears lower in the ranking, and a weighted average is also shown.
Several other country labels are not readable in the supplied image.

title: Honey Production
facts: The map shows honey production as percentages of national production by state in Mexico.
Northern, central and southern zones are labelled.
Some southern and eastern states have higher shares than many northern states.

title: 2014 Diamond Production
facts: The pie chart compares diamond production by value in 2014.
Russia is largest at 26 percent, closely followed by Botswana at 25 percent.
Canada accounts for 14 percent, Angola 9 percent and South Africa 8 percent.
Other countries together contribute 18 percent.

title: Influenced English
facts: The supplied image shows a three-dimensional pie chart with several slices.
There are three large slices and several smaller slices.
No readable category labels, legend or numerical values are visible, so exact proportions cannot be stated.

title: Gender Social Activities
facts: The bars compare men and women participating in drama, painting, sculpture and language activities.
Women are higher in drama, painting and language, while men are higher in sculpture.
Language has the largest female count at 40, while painting has the largest male count at 25.

title: Apple Life Cycle
facts: The diagram shows a repeating apple life cycle.
The labelled stages are seeds, tree, bud, flower and fruit.
The fruit supplies seeds that begin the next cycle.

title: Good and Bad Habits
facts: The illustration contrasts food and lifestyle habits using two head silhouettes.
One side shows more processed foods, while the other shows fruit and vegetables.
Diet, exercise and sleep are presented as ways to change habits and boost brainpower.

title: Television Viewing Time
facts: The histogram shows frequency by hours per day spent watching television.
The largest frequency is around 3 to 4 hours.
Very short viewing times and 6 to 7 hours are relatively uncommon.

title: Foreign Language Motivation
facts: The chart shows reasons students choose to study foreign languages.
Personal interest or enjoyment is largest at 43 percent, followed by degree requirements at 24 percent.
Future career use accounts for 13 percent, while the other reasons have smaller shares.

title: Australian Birth Trends
facts: The grouped horizontal bars compare Australian population by foreign country of birth in 2013, 2018 and 2023.
India shows the largest increase and the largest 2023 population among the countries displayed.
China is also a large group, while countries such as Brazil and Colombia have smaller totals.

title: Pet Household Owners
facts: The pie chart compares households owning different kinds of pets.
Dogs have the largest share at 45 percent, followed by cats at 29 percent.
Freshwater fish account for 8 percent and birds 6 percent, with the remaining pet categories smaller.
